title: Gate drain's 'target met' on a source check; fix places-held counter
summary: Drain stops on 'target met' from the audience rating alone, which can't catch wrong facts. I read this as two fixes: correct the places-held counter in the firstmate study (a place frees only when a worker records its ready PR or is cleaned up, per claim c3) and make model.json consistent. Then make drain's stop on target met depend on a check of the page against the pinned source, not only on the rating. The audience is the drain operator and the newcomer who reads the page.

defaults_applied.how: The cause is that the stop depends on a rating that cannot detect wrong facts, so the fix gates the stop, not only the one wrong sentence.
New drain tests cover the gate; cargo test and clippy must pass.
The check is enforced in code, not left as prose.
Behavior criteria are run with cargo test.
One focused change: the data fix plus one gate.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The wrong body text is in the firstmate-work-handling study (intro.json and model.json); I did not find a different page source.

The 'independent check' is a mechanism inside drain, such as a model-free consistency check of model.json against claims or an independent reader step, and it may reuse the existing validation rules in studies/*/validation.json.
The cheapest sound design is an extra gate on TargetMet; a full independent LLM reader inside drain is more than this change needs.
No change to athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows is needed.

acceptance_criteria.text: In studies/firstmate-work-handling/model.json the places-held counter's changed_by lists every transition that frees or takes a place (spawn t1, the ready-PR report t3, and cleanup t4), matching claim c3 and t2's retry.changes 'falls when another worker records its ready PR or is cleaned up'; the file no longer contradicts itself.
No page text in intro.json says a place is freed by anything other than a recorded PR or a cleanup; each such sentence cites c3.

Drain no longer reports Stop::TargetMet from a rating at or above the target alone: it also requires a passing check of the page against the pinned source. A test in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs shows a 4 rating with a failing check does not stop drain, and a 4 rating with a passing check does. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli`.
A test shows the check fails on the earlier contradiction (a counter's changed_by omitting a transition whose retry changes it). Run `cargo test`.
The drain report says which check held drain back when it keeps running. Run `cargo test`; `cargo clippy` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes.

out_of_scope: Re-running the study against firstmate's source
Changing the audience role's rating scale or prompt
Changing the other four drain stop reasons
departures: Slightly higher cost and lower acceptance than reference: the request is vague about what the independent check is, and it touches both data and drain logic.
